title: Pronomi Combinati
subtitle: Me lo, te lo, glielo — direct and indirect pronouns fused into one word.
objectives: Combine indirect and direct object pronouns in the correct order
Recognize the mi/ti/ci/vi → me/te/ce/ve vowel change
Recognize glielo/gliela/glieli/gliele as one fused word

content.intro: When both a direct and an indirect object pronoun appear in the same sentence — "I'll give it to you" — Italian fuses them into a single combined form, always indirect before direct.
content.explanation: Mi, ti, ci, vi change their final -i to -e before a direct object pronoun (mi + lo → me lo). Gli and le both become glie- and physically fuse with the direct pronoun into one word: gli/le + lo → glielo, gli/le + la → gliela, and so on — this single form covers "to him/her/them" plus the direct object, disambiguated only by context.
content.table:
Combined pronouns (indirect + lo/la/li/le)
Indirect+ lo+ la+ li+ le
mime lome lame lime le
tite lote late lite le
gli/leglieloglielaglieligliele
cice loce lace lice le
vive love lave live le

rules.heading: a) Order and position
rules.body: Indirect always comes first, direct second, and both go before the conjugated verb (or attach to an infinitive): Te lo do. (I give it to you.) Posso dartelo. / Te lo posso dare.

rules.heading: b) Participle agreement
rules.body: The past participle agrees with the direct object exactly as with lo/la/li/le alone: Te l'ho dato. (m. sing.) Te l'ho data. (f. sing., elided the same way)

examples.it: Il libro? Te lo do domani.
examples.en: The book? I'll give it to you tomorrow.

examples.it: Le chiavi? Gliele ho lasciate sul tavolo.
examples.en: The keys? I left them for him/her on the table.
He/she explained it to us well.
I can't tell it to you [pl.].

examples.it: Se vuoi il mio numero, te lo scrivo.
examples.en: If you want my number, I'll write it down for you.

commonMistakes.why: The indirect pronoun always comes before the direct one, and both come before the verb — never after in this order.
Gli/le physically fuse with lo/la/li/le into one written word — they never stay separate.

commonMistakes.wrong: Te l'ho dato. (for una lettera, feminine)
commonMistakes.why: The participle must agree with the feminine direct object (la lettera), even though it's now hidden inside the elided l'.

items.prompt: Il regalo? ___ do subito. (to you, tu)
La ricetta? ___ ho spiegata ieri. (to him)
items.explanation: Gli + la = gliela, fused into one word.

items.prompt: "I explained it to her" (la spiegazione, feminine)
items.explanation: Glielo/gliela fuses gli+le into one word, and the participle agrees with the feminine object.

summary: Mi/ti/ci/vi change to me/te/ce/ve before a direct object pronoun.
Gli and le both become glie-, fusing into one word: glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele.
The past participle still agrees with the direct object hidden inside the combined pronoun.
